title: Business Operating System
summary: Single product workspace that stores structured PRDs for concrete business modules before roadmap generation begins.
description: The Business Operating System is the umbrella platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, SCM, CX, GRC, ITSM, BI, work management, and marketing modules. This seed focuses on concrete PRDs that can be reviewed, approved, and later expanded into roadmap execution.

prds.title: CRM Lead Intake and Qualification

summary.oneLiner: Define the first CRM flow that captures leads, qualifies them, and promotes qualified demand into a usable pipeline record.
summary.description: This PRD covers the operational path from inbound lead creation to qualification outcome so sales teams stop managing early funnel work in spreadsheets and chat threads.
summary.whyNow: BOS needs a credible CRM foundation before opportunity, forecasting, and account planning flows can be layered on top.
summary.expectedOutcome: Sales can review lead source, ownership, qualification reason, and next action from one workflow.

problem.statement: Early-stage demand handling is fragmented and inconsistent, so qualified opportunities arrive in the pipeline without reliable source or ownership context.
problem.currentPain: Leads are copied between forms, sheets, and messaging tools. Qualification notes are often incomplete or lost.
problem.businessImpact: Sales leadership cannot trust funnel conversion metrics or coach reps from a consistent qualification standard.
problem.userImpact: Sellers waste time reconstructing context before they can act, while managers cannot tell why leads are stalling.
problem.currentWorkarounds: Teams keep manual lead sheets, forward screenshots, and rely on memory during pipeline reviews.
problem.opportunity: A structured intake and qualification workflow creates the reusable foundation for downstream CRM modules.

vision.statement: Every lead enters CRM with usable context and exits qualification with a deliberate outcome.
vision.futureState: Sales operations can inspect the whole intake funnel, and individual sellers can confidently pick up the next best lead without hidden context.
principles: Capture context once at the source

goals.title: Create controlled lead intake
goals.description: Standardize the minimum information required to create and work a lead.

goals.title: Make qualification outcomes consistent
goals.description: Require explicit outcomes, notes, and ownership changes so managers can audit funnel hygiene.

successMetrics.metric: Leads created with full required context
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Weekly audit of new lead records

successMetrics.metric: Median time from new lead to qualification decision

targetUsers.description: Works inbound leads, qualifies them, and decides whether to progress or disqualify.
Monitors funnel health and audits whether qualification standards are followed.

inScope: Lead creation with required source and owner
Lead queue filters for reps and revops

capabilities.title: Structured lead intake
capabilities.description: Create leads with enough context for a seller to act immediately.
capabilities.outcome: Every new lead enters the queue with clear source, owner, and next action.

capabilities.title: Qualification decision control
capabilities.description: Require a deliberate qualification outcome and preserve the reason behind it.
capabilities.outcome: Managers can review the funnel without guessing why leads moved or stalled.

highLevelUseCases.title: Create and assign inbound lead
highLevelUseCases.goal: Enter a new lead and immediately assign it for work
flow: Rep enters company, contact, source, and owner
System validates required fields and creates the lead
highLevelUseCases.outcome: Lead appears in the owned queue with activity history started.

highLevelUseCases.title: Qualify or disqualify a worked lead
highLevelUseCases.goal: Record a clear qualification decision after outreach
flow: Rep updates status to qualified or disqualified
Rep logs reason and next action when required
highLevelUseCases.outcome: Lead outcome is preserved for later funnel review.

requirementModel.notes: Grouped manually for the seed. Admins can regenerate after edits.

requirementItems.title: Lead must store source and owner
requirementItems.statement: Every lead record must be created with source, owner, and created timestamp.
requirementItems.reason: Without source and owner, queue accountability and reporting break immediately.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Lead creation should fail if source or owner is missing.

requirementItems.title: Lead creation requires minimum contact context
requirementItems.statement: Lead creation must require company or person name, primary contact channel, source, and owner.
requirementItems.reason: Sellers cannot act on incomplete records.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Form validation should block empty required fields.

requirementItems.title: Qualification outcome must be explicit
requirementItems.statement: A worked lead must end in qualified or disqualified state; passive abandonment is not acceptable.
requirementItems.reason: Managers need an explicit funnel outcome.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Outcome selection should be required before a lead can leave working state.

requirementItems.title: Disqualified leads require a reason
requirementItems.statement: When a lead is disqualified, the rep must choose or enter a reason.
requirementItems.reason: Disqualification patterns feed funnel quality analysis and routing improvements.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Disqualified leads should show a visible reason in list and detail view.

requirementItems.title: Lead history must show key actions
requirementItems.statement: The record should display owner changes, status changes, and notes in chronological order.
requirementItems.reason: Reps and managers need rapid context restoration.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: History should render newest-first with actor and timestamp.

requirementItems.title: Managers need queue filters by outcome and owner
requirementItems.statement: Lead list views must support filters for owner, source, stale age, and qualification outcome.
requirementItems.reason: Funnel review becomes impractical without controlled filtering.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Managers should be able to isolate stale or disqualified leads quickly.

domainRules.title: Single active owner
domainRules.rule: A lead can have only one active owner at a time.
domainRules.reason: Queue accountability depends on one clear working owner.

domainRules.title: Qualification outcome is terminal until reopened
domainRules.rule: Qualified and disqualified states are terminal unless a manager or owner deliberately reopens the lead.
domainRules.reason: Prevents accidental rework and distorted funnel metrics.

coreEntities.name: Lead
coreEntities.description: Early-stage demand record before opportunity creation.

coreEntities.name: Lead Activity
coreEntities.description: Timestamped history line for notes, owner changes, and outcome changes.

dataContext.dataOwnership: Revenue operations owns workflow policy. Sales owns execution data quality.
dataContext.dataRetentionNotes: Lead history should remain queryable for at least 24 months for funnel analysis.
dataContext.auditNeeds: Owner changes, qualification state changes, and disqualification reasons must be auditable.

uxPrinciples: Show queue-critical context in list view before opening detail
Keep qualification actions visible without hiding them in deep menus
Make reasons and next steps readable at a glance

constraints.description: Do not depend on email sync for MVP context capture.
constraints.impact: The system must still be usable if external mailbox integration is absent.

constraints.description: Queue list must remain fast for daily SDR use.
constraints.impact: Heavy interaction latency will block adoption.

dependencies.title: Workspace members and permissions
dependencies.description: Lead ownership and manager review depend on stable member identity and role access.
dependencies.riskIfMissing: Ownership and approval rules cannot be enforced cleanly.

dependencies.title: Configurable form components
dependencies.description: Lead creation relies on reusable form validation and field rendering.
dependencies.riskIfMissing: Lead intake UI becomes custom-coded and slower to evolve.

risks.title: Lead form becomes too heavy
risks.description: Adding too many required fields could slow reps and reduce adoption.
risks.mitigation: Limit MVP required fields to the minimum action-enabling set and revisit after usage review.

risks.title: Qualification reasons become inconsistent
risks.description: If reps use free text inconsistently, reporting loses comparability.
risks.mitigation: Seed a controlled reason list with optional notes instead of fully freeform input.

releaseExpectation.mvp: Manual lead intake, owner assignment, qualification outcome, and activity history.
releaseExpectation.alpha: Filtered lead queue with manager visibility and reporting-ready outcome fields.
releaseExpectation.beta: Stronger audit views, reason taxonomy tuning, and controlled reopen flow.
releaseExpectation.releaseNotes: This PRD should unlock the first reliable CRM operational dataset for BOS commercial workflows.

openQuestions.question: Who is allowed to reopen a disqualified lead?
openQuestions.context: This affects funnel hygiene, manager workflow, and user permissions.

changeLog.author: CRM Product Manager
changeLog.change: Tightened qualification outcome rules and added explicit manager filtering requirement.

changeLog.author: Sales Systems Analyst
changeLog.change: Converted discovery notes into structured personas, capabilities, and use cases.

prds.title: HRM Onboarding and Probation Control

summary.oneLiner: Create one controlled workflow for onboarding employees and managing the first probation checkpoint.
summary.description: The PRD defines the HRM flow that starts at offer acceptance, coordinates onboarding tasks, and concludes with a structured probation review checkpoint.
summary.whyNow: The business is onboarding through shared documents and ad hoc checklists, which creates inconsistent employee setup quality.
summary.expectedOutcome: HR, managers, and IT can see who owns each onboarding step and whether the employee is ready to clear probation.

problem.statement: Onboarding is distributed across messages, spreadsheets, and memory, which creates setup delays and weak probation readiness signals.
problem.currentPain: Managers do not know whether equipment, access, policy acknowledgment, and training milestones are complete.
problem.businessImpact: Time-to-productivity increases, compliance steps are missed, and probation decisions happen without evidence.
problem.userImpact: New employees receive uneven onboarding quality and experience uncertainty about expectations.
problem.currentWorkarounds: People ops keeps a manual tracker, while managers chase individual owners through chat.
problem.opportunity: A single onboarding record can later connect HR, IT, asset, learning, and manager review workflows.

vision.statement: Every new employee should move through a visible onboarding plan with explicit readiness signals for probation review.
vision.futureState: People operations, hiring managers, and support teams collaborate around one employee setup record and one shared definition of readiness.
principles: Track evidence, not just status labels
Keep manager review grounded in completed milestones

goals.title: Orchestrate onboarding work in one place
goals.description: Create one onboarding record that shows owner, due state, and completion evidence for major setup steps.

goals.title: Create a probation readiness signal
goals.description: Managers should not enter probation review without visible completion of mandatory steps.

successMetrics.metric: Employees fully set up by day one
Probation reviews backed by onboarding evidence

targetUsers.description: Owns onboarding setup and tracks completion across teams.
Reviews whether the employee is ready to clear probation and become fully productive.

capabilities.title: Onboarding control record
capabilities.description: One record that consolidates setup steps, owners, statuses, and evidence.
capabilities.outcome: People ops can inspect onboarding without stitching external trackers.

capabilities.title: Probation readiness checkpoint
capabilities.description: Present mandatory completion status before a probation review is logged.
capabilities.outcome: Managers can evaluate readiness from evidence instead of memory.

highLevelUseCases.title: Start onboarding after offer acceptance
highLevelUseCases.goal: Initialize employee setup work from one record
flow: People ops creates the onboarding record
System creates the required milestone groups
Owners can view their steps by employee and start date
highLevelUseCases.outcome: Employee onboarding is visible before day one.

highLevelUseCases.title: Run probation readiness review
highLevelUseCases.goal: See whether mandatory setup and early milestones were completed
flow: System shows mandatory milestone completion and missing evidence
Manager records probation decision or requests follow-up
highLevelUseCases.outcome: Probation review uses a visible evidence-backed summary.

requirementModel.notes: Seed grouping prepared for first review.

requirementItems.title: Employee onboarding record is mandatory
requirementItems.statement: The workflow must create one onboarding record per new employee before start date work begins.
requirementItems.reason: Without a canonical record, work remains scattered.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: System should create required onboarding sections automatically.

requirementItems.title: Mandatory steps require evidence
requirementItems.statement: Critical onboarding items must capture evidence or explicit completion notes before they are marked complete.
requirementItems.reason: Status-only onboarding hides whether real work happened.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Completion should not pass without evidence on mandatory steps.

requirementItems.title: Probation review cannot ignore missing mandatory work
requirementItems.statement: The manager review view must show incomplete mandatory steps and missing evidence before a probation decision is finalized.
requirementItems.reason: The company should not clear probation blindly.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Manager decision flow should surface blocking gaps clearly.

requirementItems.title: Managers need concise onboarding summary
requirementItems.statement: Manager-facing review should summarize completed steps, blockers, and pending owner actions without forcing deep navigation.
requirementItems.reason: Managers are not daily operators in onboarding detail views.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Review page should surface summary first and drill-down second.

domainRules.title: Mandatory day-one steps
domainRules.rule: Access, policy acknowledgment, and manager intro steps are mandatory before an onboarding record can be marked day-one ready.
domainRules.reason: These items create minimum working readiness.

coreEntities.name: Employee Onboarding Record
coreEntities.description: Primary record that tracks setup milestones and readiness state.

coreEntities.name: Onboarding Step
coreEntities.description: One owned milestone inside an onboarding record.

dataContext.dataOwnership: People operations owns workflow policy. Step owners own evidence quality.
dataContext.dataRetentionNotes: Onboarding evidence should stay available through probation and basic audit review windows.
dataContext.auditNeeds: Mandatory step completion and probation decisions must remain reviewable.

uxPrinciples: Show readiness as evidence-backed, not color-only
Keep manager summary concise and action-oriented

constraints.description: Multiple teams contribute to onboarding, so visibility must span HR, IT, and managers.
constraints.impact: Narrow ownership views would recreate shadow trackers.

dependencies.title: Workspace member identity
dependencies.description: Owner assignment depends on stable member records.

risks.title: Teams mark steps complete without evidence
risks.description: If evidence is optional in practice, the manager summary becomes untrustworthy.
risks.mitigation: Make evidence required for critical milestones and expose gaps in review UI.

releaseExpectation.mvp: Onboarding record, mandatory steps, evidence, and manager review summary.
releaseExpectation.beta: Automation reminders and deeper milestone templates.
releaseExpectation.future: Learning, asset, and equipment workflow integration.
releaseExpectation.releaseNotes: This PRD creates the first HRM execution record that can later branch into richer lifecycle flows.

openQuestions.question: Should probation summary be standardized across all roles or configurable by department?
openQuestions.context: Configurable reviews add flexibility but increase model complexity early.

changeLog.author: HR Product Manager
changeLog.change: Converted onboarding discovery into structured PRD sections and added probation gating.

prds.title: ERP Inventory Cycle Count Control

summary.oneLiner: Define the inventory cycle count flow that identifies stock variances and controls how adjustments are approved.
summary.description: This PRD covers scheduled cycle counts, variance review, and approval-gated stock adjustments so inventory accuracy work becomes auditable.
summary.whyNow: Inventory accuracy is still managed manually, and correction decisions do not have a reliable system trail.
summary.expectedOutcome: Warehouse and finance teams can trust that count variances are visible, reviewed, and approved before stock changes post.

problem.statement: Count variance handling is not consistently controlled, which weakens confidence in stock accuracy and auditability.
problem.currentPain: Supervisors record counts in sheets, adjustments happen later, and finance cannot always trace who approved the correction.
problem.businessImpact: Stock discrepancies distort replenishment, fulfillment confidence, and audit posture.
problem.userImpact: Inventory control teams spend time explaining corrections instead of preventing them.
problem.currentWorkarounds: Teams export stock data, count offline, and request approvals through chat or email.
problem.opportunity: A structured count and adjustment flow becomes a reusable control layer for broader inventory operations.

vision.statement: Inventory counts should move through one visible control path from schedule to reviewed correction.
vision.futureState: Warehouse teams can execute counts quickly, while finance and inventory control can trust the audit trail behind every variance resolution.
principles: Do not hide variance review behind spreadsheets
Require explicit approval for material corrections

goals.title: Structure cycle count execution
goals.description: Move count entry and variance visibility into the product.

goals.title: Control inventory adjustments
goals.description: Require reason and approval before material stock corrections are posted.

successMetrics.metric: Adjustment records with complete audit fields

targetUsers.description: Coordinates count schedules, reviews variances, and submits correction requests.
Reviews adjustment significance and expects reliable approval evidence.

capabilities.title: Count batch execution
capabilities.description: Run a controlled count batch and expose variance lines immediately.
capabilities.outcome: Count work stays operational while variance review becomes visible.

capabilities.title: Adjustment approval control
capabilities.description: Require approval and reason tracking before material corrections post to stock.
capabilities.outcome: Posted adjustments carry clear business evidence.

highLevelUseCases.title: Run cycle count and identify variances
highLevelUseCases.goal: Create a count batch and capture differences from expected stock
preconditions: Items and locations already exist in inventory
flow: Counters enter counted values for each line
System highlights lines where counted and expected values differ
highLevelUseCases.outcome: Variance lines are available for review before any correction occurs.

highLevelUseCases.title: Approve material adjustment
highLevelUseCases.goal: Review a requested correction before it changes stock
flow: Finance reviews reason, counted value, and proposed correction
Finance approves or rejects the adjustment
highLevelUseCases.outcome: Only approved material corrections post to inventory.

requirementModel.notes: Seed grouping for cycle count control.

requirementItems.title: Cycle counts run in structured batches
requirementItems.statement: Users must create a count batch that groups the lines to be counted together.
requirementItems.reason: Count work needs an execution container and review boundary.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Count batch must remain visible until every line is resolved.

requirementItems.title: Variances stay visible before correction
requirementItems.statement: Any mismatch between expected and counted stock must remain visible until reviewed.
requirementItems.reason: Hidden variances create weak controls and rushed adjustments.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Variance lines should display expected, counted, and difference values.

requirementItems.title: Adjustment requests require reason
requirementItems.statement: A correction request must capture the variance reason before it can be submitted.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Submission should fail when no reason is provided.

requirementItems.title: Material corrections require approval
requirementItems.statement: Corrections above the configured threshold must not post until approved.
requirementItems.reason: Material stock changes should not bypass review.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Approval state should block posting until complete.

requirementItems.title: Posted adjustments preserve audit metadata
requirementItems.statement: Posted corrections must preserve approver, timestamp, originating count line, and reason.
requirementItems.reason: Audit and reconciliation require a durable trace.
requirementItems.acceptanceHint: Audit metadata must be queryable after posting.

domainRules.title: No direct material posting
domainRules.rule: A material variance cannot post directly from count entry without review.
domainRules.reason: Separates physical counting from financial impact decisions.

coreEntities.name: Cycle Count Batch
coreEntities.description: Execution container for one scheduled count event.

coreEntities.name: Adjustment Request
coreEntities.description: Proposed stock correction created from a variance line.

dataContext.dataOwnership: Inventory control owns count execution. Finance owns approval thresholds.
dataContext.dataRetentionNotes: Adjustment evidence and approval metadata should align to stock audit retention policy.
dataContext.auditNeeds: Material correction trail must remain visible from count batch through posted stock update.

uxPrinciples: Keep count entry fast and line-based
Show variance state before any corrective action
Treat approval as a visible state, not hidden metadata

constraints.description: Count entry must remain practical on the warehouse floor.
constraints.impact: Slow or complex flows will push teams back to offline counting.

dependencies.title: Stock ledger integrity
dependencies.description: Count expectations and posted corrections rely on a trustworthy ledger.

risks.title: Approval thresholds are defined too loosely
risks.description: If materiality rules are weak, significant corrections could still move too quickly.
risks.mitigation: Agree threshold policy with finance before beta.

releaseExpectation.mvp: Cycle count batches, variance review, and approval-gated correction posting.
releaseExpectation.alpha: Supervisor dashboards and variance aging views.
releaseExpectation.beta: Role tuning and higher-volume warehouse validation.
releaseExpectation.future: RF-assisted count execution and automated recount suggestions.
releaseExpectation.releaseNotes: This PRD creates the first meaningful inventory control workflow for ERP inside BOS.

openQuestions.question: Should materiality thresholds vary by item class or only by absolute value?
openQuestions.context: Threshold logic affects approval behavior and reporting complexity.

changeLog.author: Inventory Product Manager
changeLog.change: Defined first structured PRD for cycle count and adjustment control.
